findings.body: The build fails because UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), so the zero-argument invocation cannot be resolved.
findings.failure_mode: Java compilation stops with a method-resolution error.
findings.impact: The build fails because UsernamePasswordForm only defines isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel), so the zero-argument invocation cannot be resolved.
findings.root_cause: The patch introduced a zero-argument call to a method whose only available signature requires a UserModel.
findings.suggested_fix: Call isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), or add a deliberately named zero-argument overload if that is the intended predicate.
findings.title: Pass the user argument to the conditional-passkey predicate
findings.trigger: Compiling the services module after this change.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 47 in UsernameForm.java calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments, but the only definition in UsernamePasswordForm.java (line 160) is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` requiring one argument. This will cause a compilation error.

raw_findings.body: The initial form is no longer populated with the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes and challenge, so discoverable passkeys cannot be offered or automatically used for an initial login.
raw_findings.evidence: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;
raw_findings.failure_mode: The initial login page is rendered without the data required by the browser's conditional WebAuthn flow.
raw_findings.impact: The initial form is no longer populated with the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes and challenge, so discoverable passkeys cannot be offered or automatically used for an initial login.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly introduced passkey-enabled predicate treats an unidentified user as if conditional passkeys were disabled.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not require a non-null user when deciding whether to populate the conditional-passkey form; retain only the authenticator/realm passkeys-enabled checks, while using a separate user-specific condition where needed.
raw_findings.title: Keep conditional passkeys initialized before a user is identified
raw_findings.trigger: A user opens a normal username/password login page with passkeys enabled but before any username or user has been selected.

raw_findings.body: The test treats the unexpected driver failure as proof that the WebAuthn form is absent and can pass while not actually validating the page state.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unexpected test execution failures are masked as successful negative assertions.
raw_findings.impact: The test treats the unexpected driver failure as proof that the WebAuthn form is absent and can pass while not actually validating the page state.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test catches Exception broadly around an assertion intended to accept only an absent DOM element.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Catch only NoSuchElementException (at both occurrences), preferably with assertThrows, so all other driver and assertion failures fail the test.
raw_findings.title: Do not swallow arbitrary WebDriver failures in the absence assertion
raw_findings.trigger: During either newly added WebAuthn-absence check, driver.findElement throws a WebDriverException, stale-session exception, or another unexpected Exception instead of the expected no-element exception.

finding.title: Keep conditional passkeys initialized before a user is identified
finding.trigger: A user opens a normal username/password login page with passkeys enabled but before any username or user has been selected.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that conditional passkeys won't work for initial login is incorrect. Looking at UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() lines 92-117, when context.getUser() is null (initial login), the code still calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) at line 115, which returns false when user is null, but the webauthn form setup happens in the else branch at line 103-112 regardless. The user!=null check in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled is intentional design to only enable passkeys when a user is identified.
